messages:
maria: FYI — ACME ticket: sudden embedding latency spikes and 5xxs. They say requests are being served from eu-west even though their project is pinned to na-west. Billing jump reported. cc @kevin @devon

kevin: looking now. any signs of Dedicated pool autoscale or failover?

devon: from runtime logs I'm seeing na-west queue depth >> normal for ~25m, autospillover kicked and routed to eu-west. also seeing mixed 401/503/200 sequences in the customer's trace.

maria: ticket includes this curl output (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" -H "x-region: na-west" https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token"}

# retry
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" -H "x-region: na-west" https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"runtime_unavailable"}

# then a request routed to eu-west that succeeds
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" -H "x-region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

ajay: token scoping note: tokens minted for na-west projects are region-scoped unless project is org-global. When routing falls back to a different region we do a service-token exchange. If that exchange fails the request should 401, not 503. need to check auth-exchange logs.

sophie: pulling auth logs — exchange service returned 403 for many of the failing traces. Missing or wrong `aud` claim for eu-west. looks like the exchange attempted with an old signing key during rotation window.

linh: we rotated signer keys yesterday at 03:00 UTC. routing proxies have a key-cache TTL of 10m; under normal load that syncs, but with heavy queueing some frontends still had stale keys. combine that with rapid retries and you get exchange failures.

kevin: why are we seeing 503s from runtime then? if auth fails it should be 401 as ajay said.

devon: 503s are from runtime because when fallback kicks the runtime tried to pull model prefix/KV from cross-region store and hit a network timeout. so sequence: 1) original region auth fails (401), 2) fallback triggers runtime to proxy to eu-west, 3) cross-region KV timeout -> 503, 4) later eu-west handles request and returns 200 for some requests. messy.

maria: customer wants immediate mitigation and RCA. can we get short-term fixes?

ajay: short-term mitigations:
- if customer agrees, manually pin them to na-west to prevent cross-region fallback (only if na-west capacity can be increased)
- hot-add capacity to na-west (spin up 2x g4 nodes temporarily)
- force key-sync across all auth proxies / revert rotation if needed
- add temporary routing rule to avoid cross-region fallback for region-scoped tokens

sophie: I'm pushing a key-sync to auth proxies now. will post when finished.

kevin: I'll file a routing-policy follow-up so we don't drop into auth loops during fallbacks. long-term we should validate token compatibility before fallback.

linh: repro plan (will run from staging):
1) set project region=na-west and region-scope tokens on a test org
2) flood na-west with concurrent embeddings requests at 200qps for 10m to force queueing
3) observe routing decisions, auth-exchange behavior, and runtime KV timeouts
4) collect trace ids and logs: routing, auth-exchange, runtime

maria: can infra accelerate capacity? customer is on SE escalation.

infra-bot: scheduled capacity increase in na-west: add 2x g4 instances. ETA ~30m unless blocked. React :thumbsup: to confirm.

devon: tailing logs now, capturing trace ids from the customer's ticket. will correlate with auth and runtime traces after key-sync.

csm-alex: I'll ask ACME to approve temporary pinning and explain billing implications. also tracking the spike for credits discussion.

maria: thanks team. I'll update the customer and keep thread updated with repro results and any mitigation timelines.
